title: Client-phased toolframe proposal (sketch)
content:
Purpose

Sketch-level PRD describing a client-phased toolframe approach: small, composable response frames emitted by the Hosted API that let client SDKs perform progressive rendering, tool invocation, and resume/snapshot semantics with explicit fidelity lanes. This is a product-facing draft: scope is SDK surface, streaming frames, and structured toolcall lifecycle for the Hosted API.

Problem statement

- Many client integrations want: incremental UI updates, deterministic tool invocation points, and the ability to cheaply resume/resume-snapshots across unreliable networks.
- Current full-response or raw token streams either force client-side parsing complexity (ad-hoc heuristics) or require heavyweight client-side orchestration.
- Tool calling semantics are brittle in partial responses: duplicate tool calls, ambiguous commit points, and poor telemetry for per-call latencies.

Goals

1) Define a compact streaming frame that: conveys partial natural language text, marks toolcall intents with stable ids, and optionally carries structured payloads (JSON schema).
2) Define an SDK contract (JS/py) with 3 phased responsibilities: hydrate, enact, finalize. Minimal surface to reduce cognitive load.
3) Built-in resume/snapshot: lightweight incremental checkpointing so clients can reconnect and rehydrate without duplicating tool side-effects.
4) Telemetry hooks: per-frame tracing ids, backpressure signals and cost-attribution breadcrumbs (token counts, model variant).

Non-goals

- Not addressing full offline-first client caches or local model execution.
- Not standardizing a final schema for all structured outputs; this is a framing for versioned schema bundles.

User stories

- Frontend engineer: need UX that shows partial answers + an actionable button returned as soon as intent is recognized (e.g., "open-ticket"). She wants no custom parsing and an SDK event when action becomes available.
- Mobile app: intermittent connectivity. App must resume a streaming session and display committed actions without reissuing tool calls.
- Platform integrator: needs per-tool latency and successful/failed counts surfaceable to Console.

High-level design: phased toolframes

- Frame types (compact names): TEXT, TOOL_INTENT, TOOL_RESULT, CHECKPOINT, META
- Each frame is newline-delimited JSONL over streaming socket/HTTP chunked; frames are small (<4KB typical).
- TEXT frames contain incremental text fragments with offset and sequence_id; clients append in order.
- TOOL_INTENT frames contain: tool_name, tool_id (stable per-session), suggested_args (schema uri or inline), confidence_hint, and commit_window (ms). The SDK must expose an event handler for this frame.
- TOOL_RESULT frames are produced after a tool executes (either by client or server-side tool shim). Contains tool_id, status, result_payload (optionally signed/opaque).
- CHECKPOINT frames include minimal resume tokens and last_applied_tool_id; CHECKPOINTs are emitted periodically or on explicit commit.
- META frames include billing hints (token_delta, model_variant), and tracing parent ids.

Why phased vs monolithic?

- Phased frames separate recognition (when model signals an intent) from action (when tool executes) and from finalization (when result is committed). This prevents duplicate runs when clients reconnect and simplifies deterministic replay.

SDK ergonomics (JS first pass)

Surface: new StreamingClient + small callback API. Example pseudocode:

const stream = client.startStreaming({prompt})
stream.on('text', (frag) => render.append(frag.text))
stream.on('tool_intent', (intent) => showAction(intent.id, intent.preview))
stream.on('checkpoint', (cp) => storeLocal(cp.token))

Decisions for ergonomics:
- Default behavior: SDK will NOT auto-execute tool intents. Rationale: avoid surprising side-effects; explicit call = safe.
- Helper: sdk.executeTool(tool_id, args) -> returns promise that resolves when TOOL_RESULT frame observed; SDK handles idempotency tokens and retry heuristics.
- Optional mode: server-side toollet execution where SDK asks server to run an approved tool (for small managed integrations). This is opt-in via request flags.

Resume / snapshot behavior

- Clients can reconnect by sending last_checkpoint token; server will stream frames starting after that checkpoint. Server guarantees no TOOL_INTENT will be re-emitted with identical tool_id unless it was not acknowledged (client must ack TOOL_RESULT by id).
- Checkpoint token is opaque but stable for a session. It must encode last_applied_tool_id and sequence cursor.

Structured output and schema bundles

- Toolkit: allow frames to reference a schema_uri (versioned bundle hosted by Redwood). The schema bundle contains example payloads, validation rules and optional client-side render hints.
- When a TOOL_RESULT includes result_payload with schema_uri, SDK validates (best effort) and surfaces structured data via stream.on('structured', data).
- Schema compatibility: server will include schema_version in META frames; SDKs should warn on mismatch.

Backpressure and pacing

- Clients can emit a small numeric backlog hint in request_metadata (max_pending_frames) to instruct server runtime to prefer low-latency single-token TEXT frames vs larger batches.
- Server can send FLOW_CONTROL frames with suggested window sizes. SDK should buffer and surface a prefetching indicator so UI can degrade gracefully.

Security and safety considerations

- Tool intents are not execution grants. Execution must be authorized by token-permission checks. If opt-in server-side tool execution is used, server must validate client permission and produce signed TOOL_RESULT frames.
- Structured payloads may contain PII — metadata includes redact_flags and a pointer to redact-policy applicable; Console will surface redaction sampling.

Observability & Console integration

- Each frame contains trace_id and frame_id. Console can reconstruct per-request timelines, per-tool latencies, and checkpoint frequency.
- Billing attribution: META frames include token_delta and model_variant; Console aggregates to show per-tool cost impact.

Migration and rollout plan

Phase 0 (internal): Spec + prototype SDK JS + server runtime opt-in flag. End-to-end test w/ 3 sample tools.
Phase 1 (beta): Expose in Hosted API with experimental header X-RW-Frame=phased-v1; opt-in roam. Invite select customers and integrate Console telemetry.
Phase 2 (GA): Default for new streaming endpoints and SDKs, schema bundle public registry, and migration tooling for older clients.

Open questions / risks

- Checkpoint token semantics need to be clearly spec'd for cross-region failover. Does token tie to infra node? (ops input)
- Idempotency semantics for tools that have external side-effects (e.g., send-email). We propose: require server-signed receipts + client acking; but need legal/CS input for contract.
- How large should frames be? Small frames are lower-latency but higher overhead; need perf experiments.
- Mobile offline UX: checkpoints reduce duplication but UI story for uncommitted intents needs design.

Next steps / action items

- Engineering (serving-runtime): perf experiment ticket to measure tokenized overhead for 512 vs 2KB frames (ticket JIRA-STREAM-233).
- Product: draft beta invite criteria and data retention (owner: Priya).
- DX: prototype JS SDK with minimal API and sample app (owner: Marco).
- Legal/CS: review idempotency and signed-tool-result contract (owner: Lina).

Notes to self / rough ideas

- Consider a compact binary frame variant for mobile (protobuf-lite) to cut overhead.
- Maybe use monotonic integer tool_id combined with uuid session for readability.
- Could be useful to support a "preview_action" TTL (e.g., auto-expire intents if not acted within n seconds).

Reference sketches and links in linked_artifacts.

End of sketch.
